title: Roots of an integral polynomial are carried along ring homomorphisms
statement: Let $P\in\mathbf Z[T]$, let $K$ and $L$ be commutative rings (in the application, fields), and let $\varphi:K\to L$ be a ring homomorphism. Write $P^{(K)}\in K[T]$ and $P^{(L)}\in L[T]$ for the coefficientwise extensions of $P$ along the unique ring homomorphisms $\mathbf Z\to K$ and $\mathbf Z\to L$. If $x\in K$ satisfies $P^{(K)}(x)=0$, then $P^{(L)}(\varphi(x))=0$.

source.place: statement, clause 'Then $\jmath_{\ell'}(\alpha)$ is a reciprocal root of $P_{i,\ell'}$' (asserted; the ## Proof gives no argument for it)
